name: Review content ideas against your existing pages with HasData, OpenAI and Google Sheets

values.skipSelectors: script, style, nav, header, footer, noscript

parameters.content:
# Check a content idea before writing another article

### How it works
Enter one proposed topic in Settings. The workflow compares it with text from pages in your sitemap scope and a current Google SERP. It recommends updating an existing page, proposing a new page, leaving covered content alone, or requesting more research. Google Sheets stores the recommendation, evidence and reviewer decision; it is not a batch input queue.

Code attaches original source passages and checks source IDs, target URLs and output structure. It does not verify the model's interpretation. Review the evidence yourself.

Sitemap discovery, page reads and model input have limits. Partial coverage cannot produce an automatic create-new recommendation. The workflow does not prove cannibalization or guarantee a complete site inventory. It does not write or publish articles.

### Setup
Install the verified HasData community node. Connect HasData credentials to both request nodes, OpenAI to both model requests, and Google Sheets to all three Sheets nodes. Create a Review queue tab using the column names in the nearby review-state note. Set site, same-host XML sitemap, path prefix, query and spreadsheet_id in Settings. Start with max_pages = 3 and mode = analyze.

To request a brief, set approval to APPROVED and decision to update_existing or create_new in Sheets. Explain decision overrides in editor_notes. Run mode = brief with the same site, path, query and location. Clear an existing brief explicitly before regenerating.

### Customization
Change location, limits, content_selector and model in Settings. Run one execution at a time; do not edit its row during analysis. HasData and OpenAI charge for usage. Automatic paid retries are disabled.

## 1. Configure one idea
Enter the topic in Settings, not Sheets. Validate the site, sitemap and request limits before reading external data.

## 2. Check this idea's review state
Existing approvals and briefs block re-analysis.

Create these columns in Review queue:
`idea_key`, `query`, `scope`, `decision`, `target_url`, `intent`, `rationale`, `gaps`, `next_action`, `evidence_json`, `coverage`, `pages_read`, `pages_discovered`, `serp_request_id`, `checked_at`, `approval`, `editor_notes`, `brief`, `brief_created_at`

## 3. Read the sitemap
Read a URL list or one index level. Only same-host HTTPS URLs are eligible. A sitemap does not guarantee a complete site inventory.

## 4. Resolve page sources
Fetch direct child sitemaps or reuse the root URL list. Nested indexes and exceeded limits mark coverage partial. Failed sitemap requests stop the run.

## 5. Read bounded page text
Prioritize URLs, fetch up to max_pages with HasData, then extract content_selector. URL words only order the crawl; they do not establish topic coverage.

## 6. Check extraction and collect SERP evidence
Record failed and truncated page reads, then fetch search results. This step checks text availability, not whether the topic is covered. Snippets are not search-volume data.

## 7. Evaluate, validate and save
The model proposes a decision. Code checks source IDs, inspected target URLs and output structure, then attaches original passages. Partial coverage blocks automatic create_new. Review the interpretation in Sheets; source validation does not prove it correct.

## 8. Draft only after approval
Set approval to APPROVED and decision to update_existing or create_new in Sheets. Explain overrides in editor_notes. Switch Settings to brief with the same context. Saves a draft, not an approved document. No new HasData requests or publishing.
